Practical reading: if a position list is meant to agree with a behavioural search, use a positive objective on their prompts and equalise layers; our contrastive J2 list is optimised for our readout and should not be sold as behaviour-recovering. Sampling-surface test (plan 2.39.2, 60 recipes x 4 prompt surfaces built only from published text; results/objective_surface.json). My registered prediction - exact overlap rises with the number of surfaces - is FALSIFIED: exact overlap at K = their neuron count is 1.67% for 1, 2, 3 and 4 surfaces alike (one recipe out of 60 at every depth). What does move is the neighbourhood: recipes with at least one of their coordinates inside our top-64 go 51.7% -> 56.7% -> 60.0% -> 60.0%, at a median rank of 11-12, and the sign agreement is 98.5-98.9% on this subset (93.4% on the full 178). So the three questions separate cleanly and should never be conflated again: the DIRECTION is reproducible (93-99%), the NEIGHBOURHOOD covers half to 60% of recipes, and the exact 1-4 coordinate LIST is not recoverable (1.67%, invariant to surfaces). The residual gap is methodological, not a sampling artefact: their coordinates are found by reading which neuron WRITES the behaviour's words in the steer lens and then validating behaviourally, whereas a first-order gradient ranks coordinates by marginal log-probability gain - and under joint/threshold effects (their own record: a 6+1 sum measured at 16, 2.3x superadditive) those are different orderings. Deliverable boundary to state publicly: we can claim positions supported by the algebra AND the three external instruments, and signs that agree with behavioural doses to 93-99%, but we must NOT claim to recover a behaviourally-searched coordinate set. Second-order probe (plan 2.39.3, 12 recipes, exact per-token Fisher in residual space where the budget metric is the identity; results/objective_second_order.json). Hypothesis tested: the residual gap after 2.39.2 is the objective's CURVATURE (joint/threshold effects their recipes show, 2.3x superadditivity). Result: not confirmed - second order makes the neighbourhood WORSE, not better. Recipes with at least one of their coordinates inside our top-64: plain |g| (first order, coordinate metric) 58.3%, umag (first order, budget metric) 16.7%, second order 25.0%/16.7%/16.7% at mu=0.3/1/3. What curvature does buy is the RANK when a coordinate does appear (median 7-14 against 28 for |g|), so it narrows without widening. Exact overlap at K = their count is 0/12 here (1/60 in the 60-recipe run, so that column is noise at this sample size). Sign agreement stays 95.1% (12 recipes), consistent with 93.4% over 178 and 98.5% over 60 - direction is stable across every variant, and positions are what changes. Interpretation, now with three independent probes behind it: the community's pipeline finds SEMANTICALLY NAMEABLE coordinates (steer-lens: which neuron writes the word) and validates behaviourally, while our closed form finds the coordinates with the most effect per unit residual budget; the budget-metric correction is exactly what moves us off their picks, and that same correction is what wins +25.8% on OUR readout (2.36 K=256). Hence reproducing their coordinates is the wrong objective for our method - it would trade away our own advantage.

The correct quantity is the noise-to-signal ratio tr(Sigma)/||g||^2 (McCandlish et al.'s gradient noise scale), of which isotropy is the special case d*v.

plan258_icc_math.why: the half-sum cosine r = (||S||^2 - sum||x_i||^2)/(||S||^2 + sum||x_i||^2) writes the signal as a difference of two quantities of the same order that leaves ~10% behind (measured: 0.174 - 0.155 = 0.019), so any COMMON-MODE perturbation (a bias shared by every rollout of a batch) lands in the numerator at first order. That is why r moved 0.0685 -> 0.2704 when the gradients were computed in a batch, with every individual vector agreeing to cos 0.999.

Directions agree across groups (cos 0.6554 vs 0.6500; ratio 0.796 vs 0.907); the scale does not (||g||^2 differs 4x and the seed-0 point estimate lies below its own interval), so directions reproduce and the sample requirement does not at 8 contexts. (3) kappa was read as the sample requirement; r(K)=K/(K+2*kappa) makes that 2*kappa, so K(0.5) = 435/377 from curves and 4201/1004 from pooled 2*kappa - quoted as 10^2-10^3. (5) plan252 takes every number from closed_form_v3.json (gfile p_a2_v2.pt, SELF residuals 2.52e-5/1.99e-5, dJ2_pw 2.76527/4.77902). 0.58.0 (ICC mathematics, Lean-verified): the reliability estimator is being replaced by the classical intraclass correlation because the half-sum cosine is ill-conditioned in exactly the direction of batch bias. Two declarations, axioms exactly {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, opl-leancheck PROVED: ssw_shift_invariant (the within-group sum of squares is exactly invariant under a common-mode shift - the property the plug-in lacks) and icc_bounds (the ICC lies in [-1/(n-1), 1] for MSb>=0<MSw, n>=2). Lean refuted my first statement: at MSb = 0 the ICC EQUALS the lower bound, so that side must be <=, not <; the formalisation found a real error in the claim I was about to publish. The estimator is NOT yet implemented in scripts/reliability.py and no number has been recomputed with it, which is stated in metadata.plan258_icc_math. 0.59.0 (tensorised pipeline, money-driven): the pipeline now batches the score arm (per-sample gradients read from the same delta leaf) and the 2K pathwise pairs (chunked 8), computes column norms on the GPU, and does the reliability analysis from ONE Gram matrix. Wall clock for 8 contexts x 32 rollouts: 6-8 min -> 52 s, GPU mean 44-59% instead of mostly 0%. Conclusion at this n: reliability is NOT resolved, and the earlier plug-in r(K) (0.07-0.27) measured shared batch bias rather than reliability. A defect was found during the re-run: split_half_curve_fast weighted the Gram on one side only, so its 'cosines' exceeded 1 (1.82, 4.71); it is fixed (Mw @ Mw.T) but those numbers must not be quoted until re-run. The ICC path is unaffected because gram_from_scores weights both sides. 0.61.0 (Lean modularised, from the engineering criticism): the single lean/Reliability.lean was split into one file per theorem group - Ssw.lean (R1 shift invariance), Icc.lean (R2 bound + R4 SS_b >= 0 by construction, which discharges R2 hypothesis), Witness.lean (R5: the plug-in squared cosine moves 0 -> 1/2 under a common shift). Five declarations, all PROVED with axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, each file compiled on its own. Three consecutive breakages had come from editing a single 91-line file by string slicing; R5 had failed twice for a missing `open scoped InnerProductSpace`, which is invisible in a monolith. R3 (the code's NORMALISED form) remains unformalised and is recorded as such in results/lean_audit.json. 0.62.0 (R3): lean/SswNormalised.lean proves the code's NORMALISED within-group quantity is shift-invariant - the gap Ssw.lean left. The technical blocker was rewrite order inside the smul expansion (norm_smul / Real.norm_eq_abs / abs_of_pos must precede ring). What is STILL missing and is explicitly recorded: the ANOVA decomposition ss_t − ss_w = k·Σ_c‖x̄_c − x̄‖², so the code's subtraction is not yet tied to the nonnegative quantity R4 describes; and the F-quantile implementation is unverified. 0.63.0 (ANOVA, partial): lean/Mean.lean proves the deviations from the group mean sum to zero, and lean/SsDecomp.lean proves the per-group split Σ‖f−g‖² = Σ‖f−mean f‖² + K‖mean f−g‖² — the mathematical heart of the decomposition that ties the code's SUBTRACTION to the nonnegative between-group quantity. Both PROVED, axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. Unblocked by fixing a rewrite direction (smul_smul is a • (b • x) = (a*b) • x; I had used ←). verdict.meaning: L14N8949 is a real, directional, dose-monotone lever that does act on the hostility readout: J2 (hostility-vs-neutral slot mass) rises +0.0059/+0.0095/+0.0191/+0.0484 over doses 0.005-0.05, positive on 6/6 held-out probes at 0.02, 8x the same-layer random control mean at 0.02 and 32x at 0.05, and the mirrored arm is negative and growing (so not a generic perturbation). What is NOT shown is exclusivity: on 3 shared contexts it never ranks first among the five hand-written trait contrasts. Two caveats keep that from being a refutation: (i) the coordinate came from one brute-force generation-based scan, i.e. a draw, not the optimum of any hostility criterion; (ii) n=3 contexts with wide per-trait spread cannot separate "not specific" from "specific but small".
verdict.S2_note: pre-registered rule not met (hostility never the max of five traits, 3/3 contexts). Power is low: 3 contexts, per-trait sd 0.011-0.044, hostility mean 0.0275 with 95% CI [-0.025, +0.080]; hostility ranks 2nd in one context (0.048 vs 0.067). So this run does not show "not hostility-specific"; it shows specificity is undemonstrated.
verdict.S2_instrument_note: The pre-registered S2 used the J1 five-trait matrix, whose five contrasts share one neutral negative; it therefore measures evaluative register, not specificity. The within-instrument test (two J2 readouts, hostile-vs-praise and praise-vs-neutral) shows the opposite of a uniform lift: h-n up, c-n down, 8/8 coordinates and dose-monotone. So S2 FAIL is an instrument result, not evidence about the coordinate.
